Items.Authors: José Leonardo Garcés Medina, Gerardo Lara Lucario, Carolina Keiman
Items.Title: Modernization of the FRIDA cold test facility cryostat: migration from a legacy PLC architecture to a modular monitoring and protection platform
Items.Abstract: The FRIDA Cold Test Facility (FCTF), a cryostat used extensively for the early validation of subsystems later integrated into the near-infrared instrument FRIDA, lacks many of the operational and safety features now standard in modern cryogenic systems. In contrast, the larger FRIDA cryostat -cycled more than ten times during integration- implements advanced house-keeping capabilities, including robust interlocks, structured data logging, automated thermal-cycle control, web-based monitoring, and messaging-bot alerts. We present a modernization of FCTF that incorporates these proven technologies into a new control architecture featuring a re-engineered control layer, an independent fail-safe interlock system, a supervisory server with automated procedures, real-time dashboards, and an alert-notification service. The upgrade transforms FCTF into a safer, more reliable, and more versatile platform for testing future cryogenic subsystems.

Items.Authors: Miguel Andrés Sánchez Carrasco, M. Carmen Pastor Morales, Juan Manuel Gómez López, Rosario Sanz Mesa, Julio F. Rodríguez Gómez, Nicolás Robles Muñoz, Francisco Lobón Villanueva, Sylvain Ranvier, Jean-Charles Matéo-Vélez, Rémi Pacaud, Michel Anciaux
Items.Title: Modular thermo-mechanical framework for agile prototyping of space instruments: the DUSTER case
Items.Abstract: The paper describes the thermo-mechanical framework developed for the DUSTER breadboard, aimed at integrating EMI-sensitive, high-voltage electronics in a configuration that remains practical for assembly and test. The enclosure is built from stacked aluminium frames supporting the DPU, the low- and high-voltage power supplies, and the sensor front-ends. Connector distribution was arranged to limit cable cross-routing and to keep kilovolt-level bias lines away from low-level analog paths. EMC control relies on conductive gaskets at the critical interfaces, while the thermal design follows a staged approach based on board-level conduction, internal heat links, and external baseplate coupling. This made it possible to introduce thermal improvements during laboratory testing without redesigning the enclosure.

Items.Authors: Francesco Di Mille, Marcelo Mora, Nicole David, Povilas Palunas
Items.Title: Monitoring instrument throughput at the Magellan Telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present an ongoing program to monitor the efficiency and throughput of the Magellan telescopes and their facility instruments. Standard stars and fields observed as part of routine operations are used to derive photometric zero points and spectroscopic efficiencies on a regular cadence. In parallel, the reflectivity of the primary, secondary, and tertiary mirrors is measured as part of the regular Magellan mirror-maintenance program, providing an estimate of the total telescope reflectivity. By correlating changes in mirror reflectivity and maintenance events with variations in instrument sensitivity, we link the state of the telescope optics directly to the overall response of the instrument suite. We present these correlations for individual instruments and discuss their use in tracking instrument health, validating performance after cleaning or recoating, and quantifying the long-term stability of system throughput across the facility.

Items.Authors: Marco Falotico, Guido Agapito, Paolo Ciliegi, Giuseppe Notarstefano
Items.Title: MORFEO at ELT: control strategies for tip-tilt compensation on extremely large telescopes
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics  module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments:  MICADO and HARMONI.  Compensation of Tip and Tilt modes of aberration is a key challenge on Extremely Large Telescopes like the  ELT, and on its Adaptive Optics module, MORFEO. Because of the large telescope structure and the wind  effects, Tip-Tilt disturbances have large power at very low frequencies, and may present resonant peaks related to  mechanical oscillations. In this work we analyze different control strategies for Tip-Tilt compensation, including  pure integrators, which may not be suited for accurate loop shaping, Infinite Impulse Response filters with online  gain optimization, and Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controllers. Frequency shaping of the LQG is investigated, to  recover stability margins of the closed loop in a measurement feedback scenario.

Items.Authors: Alfio Puglisi, Andrea Baruffolo, Giulio Capasso, Chiara Di Prospero, Salvatore Lampitelli, Amedeo Petrella, Salvatore Savarese, Danilo Selvestrel
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: design of the soft real-time computer
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The module provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. MORFEO includes twelve separate wavefront sensors, two internal post-focal deformable mirrors, and it must coordinate the operation of the ELT M4 deformable mirror and six laser launcher units. While the data flow between these devices is handled by a dedicated real-time core, the Soft Real-Time Computer plays a fundamental role in system coordination, optimization, and interfacing with the rest of the instrument, in addition handling of special features like M4 segmentation and data recording for engineering and scientific purposes. This paper describes the design choices made to handle this complexity, while remaining within the bounds of the ESO-provided RTC Toolkit as dictated by telescope harmonization strategies.

Items.Authors: Chiara Di Prospero, Alfio T. Puglisi, Andrea Baruffolo, Giulio Capasso, Salvatore Lampitelli, Salvatore Savarese
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: prototyping activities of MORFEO soft real time computer towards ESO final design review
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  This paper details the prototyping activities for the MORFEO Soft Real Time Computer (SRTC), validating its architecture for stringent timing requirements and instrument functionalities, as presented at the ESO Final Design Review (FDR).  Using a hardware testbed and the ESO rtc-toolkit framework, three prototypes were developed:  1.A distributed full telemetry system managing high throughput via network separation (VLANs), real-time scheduling, and NUMA-aware resource allocation  2.Benchmarking of auxiliary loop algorithms in Python and C++, establishing the need for parallel computing and GPU acceleration  3.Customization of rtc-toolkit modules to meet instrument needs while preserving performance  The final SRTC design is based on these prototypes.

Items.Authors: Matteo De Magistris, Marcello Agostino Scalera, Paolo Ciliegi, Andrea Di Rocco
Items.Title: MORFEO@ELT system engineering toward FDR
Items.Abstract: Morfeo (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is an adaptive optics module able to compensate the wavefront disturbances affective the scientific observation. It will be installed on the straight-through port of the telescope Nasmyth platform to serve the first-light instrument MICADO and with the provision for a future second instrument. The module underwent the Preliminary Design Review in 2021 and is starting now the FDR process.  In this paper we present a synthesis of the System Engineering approach adopted to manage the development of the instrument assessing the criticalities of phase C (final design) and beginning of phase D (Early procurement. We will discuss the evolution of the system engineering approach, identifying within the MBSE framework the evolution of the various modelling artefacts. towards the requirements. We will detail the criticalities of the system engineering with a particular focus onto the management of the interfaces between subsystem

Items.Authors: Julien Dejonghe, Nick Cvetojevic, Diane Chapuis Kerouanton, Tim Morris, Jürgen Schmoll, Nazim Ali Bharmal, Ian Lewis
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: concept proposal for a telescope beam simulator and alignment tool for MOSAIC
Items.Abstract: The ELT scale, combined with the accuracy required at visible and near-infrared wavelengths, leads to new challenges in terms of optical alignment.  MOSAIC uses the full field of view of the ELT, with 300 positioners redirecting light towards science paths. Four GLAO systems are able to acquire sub-fields and LED targets located on Focal Plane. Therefore, the sky is linked to the structure supporting the optics at focal plane. Nevertheless, as MOSAIC is dedicated to the observation of very faint objects, some science paths must work in a so-called “blind” mode: long exposures are necessary to get signal from the observed object. Active tracking on science beams is then difficult, and some challenging science requirements in term of pointing accuracy leads to define a co-alignment strategy, optically linking GLAO with the science paths.  This poster presents an alignment tool or ELT beam simulator concept, allowing high-precision optical alignment and proper look-up table building.

Items.Authors: Kacem El Hadi, Myriam Rodrigues, Diane Chapuis, Laurent Martin, Marc Jaquet, Alexandre Bozier, Bruno Castilho, Timothy J. Morris, Nazim Ali Bharmal, Ian J. Lewis, Markus Thurneysen, Maxime Rombach, Julien Dejonghe, Ana Pérez Calpena, Meghna Mohamed, Marie Larrieu, Michel Dupieux, Clément Hottier, Franck Ducret, Thomas Augusteijn, Gavin Dalton, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Alessandro Meoli, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Jay Stephan, Ruben Jansen, Christian Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: instrument AITV strategies
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the Muti-Object Spectrograph for the 39m ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument development has recently been reorganized in different channels to be implemented progressively.  The Laboratoire d’Astrophysique de Marseille (LAM) is in charge of the instrument “Assembly, Integration, Test and Verification (AIT/V)” phases. AITV for AO instruments, in laboratory or at the telescope, always represent numerous technical challenges. We already started the preparation and planning for the instrument level AIT activities, from identification of needs, challenges, risks, to defining the the instrument AITV strategies.  In this paper, we present the state of this study, discuss the instrument integration & test options, all depending of the availability of any European AIT facility to host the full instrument. We describe a basline option with the full instrument test as well as new approach with distributed AIT activities and controlled remotely over different European sites.

Items.Authors: Zalpha Challita, Alexandre Bozier, Yannick Charles, Léo Defever, Johan Floriot, Anne-Sophie Hutter, Tony Pamplona, Patrice Sanchez, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Kacem El Hadi, Jesús Gallego Maestro, Mathieu Puech, Roser Pello
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: overview of the MAIT strategy of an athermal camera prototype for the NIR-spectrograph
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object spectrograph (MOS) for the ESO 39m European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The instrument is progressing in phase B2 since 2025. It presents multi-object and multi-integral field spectroscopy capabilities and combines visible and near-infrared channels, to observe from resolved stars up to the most distant galaxies. The two NIR-spectrographs (130K-80K) are part of the NIR-channel system led by the Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM, Spain). The current design includes four camera modules delivered by the Laboratoire d’Astrophysique de Marseille (LAM, France), two per spectrograph, ensuring the spectral coverage of the two observing bands J (0.95-1.34 μm) and H (1.43-1.8 μm). Each camera is equipped with Teledyne H4RG detectors (4kx4k, 15 μm pixels). This paper presents the MAIT strategy and development to verify the athermal concept of a cryogenic NIR camera prototype in relevant environment (ESO TRL5) and to anticipate the MAIT plan of the NIR cameras.

Items.Authors: Jay Stephan, Mathieu Puech, Rubén Sánchez Janssen, Myriam Rodrigues, Armando Gil de Paz, Nicolas Laporte, Søren Larsen, Timothy J. Morris, Roser Pello, Thomas Augusteijn, Gavin B. Dalton, Kacem El Hadi, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Marie Larrieu, Alessandro Meoli, Hermine Schnetler, Christian Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: status of science requirements and trade-off studies
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object spectrograph (MOS) for the 39-meter Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) of the European Southern Observatory (ESO). It offers unique capabilities in observing modes (single-object and integral field unit), multiplexing, wavelength coverage, and spectral resolution. Designed to operate in both the visible and near-infrared domains, MOSAIC maximises coverage of the ELT focal plane (~40 arcmin²). It is optimised to deliver the highest possible signal-to-noise ratio for the faintest sources, from stars in our Galaxy to galaxies at the epoch of reionisation. This paper outlines the methodology for translating top-level science requirements into instrument specifications. It summarises the key trade-off studies on sky coverage, trace separation, atmospheric dispersion, and airglow saturation, conducted in preparation for the System Architecture Review, which was completed between April and June 2025

Items.Authors: Bruno V. Castilho, Décio Ferreira, André G. Coutinho, Antonio B. Braulio Neto, Bruno S. Pinto, Leandro H. dos Santos, Eleonai L. Barbedo, Lucimara Martins, Milena Lusa, Marc Jacquet, Laurent Martin, Alexandre Bozier, Diane Chapuis, Kacem El Hadi, Beatriz S. Barbuy, Thomas Augusteijn, Gavin B. Dalton, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Marie Larrieu, Alessandro Meoli, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Myriam Rodrigues, Ruben Sanchez -Janssen, Hermine Schnetler, Jay Stephan, Christian Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: the instrument core subsystem (ICOS) design status
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC, the wide-field multi-object spectrograph for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), is  advancing through Phase B2, where subsystem architectures mature toward the Preliminary  Design Review. Central to the Front-End channel is the Instrument Core System (ICOS), which  provides the mechanical support, alignment stability, and controlled rotation required by the  focal-plane assembly and the GLAO, ORSS, and CALEMOS subsystems. ICOS comprises a steel  Static Structure Module interfaced to the Nasmyth platform, a motorized Rotating Structure  Module that delivers field-rotation compensation with ≤0.095 mrad accuracy, and a Cable Wrap  Module enabling continuous ±180° motion. ICOS must include an alignment strategy capable of restoring the optical axis to the sub-100µm level required for injection efficiency and pupil stability. With refined interfaces and a mass near 13.4 t, ICOS is converging toward a robust preliminary design for Phase C.

Items.Authors: Nick Cvetojevic, Julien Dejonghe, Nicolas Mauclert, Paul Girard, Yan Caujolle, Olivier Boebion, Daniel Lecron, Stephane Lagarde, Diane Chapuis, Kacem El Hadi
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: the optical relay sub-system (ORSS)
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object fibre spectrograph for ESO's 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). It offers unique capabilities for a gigantic telescope in terms of multiplexing, wavelength coverage, and spectral resolution. One of MOSAIC’s observation modes is to position up to 8 independent fibre Integral Field Units (IFUs) anywhere withing the ~ 40 arcmin^2 field of view. To achieve this, each of MOSAIC’s positioners has an additional pick-off mirror that can redirect the light to the instrument’s edge and into the Optical Relay Sub-System (ORSS) modules that will inject in into the IFU fibre bundles, and enable the mIFU observation mode of MOSAIC. The module requirement is to ensure the image plane is at the correct place regardless of the targets position in the focal plane and must correct for up to 1m of optical path difference. In this paper we outline the latest optical and mechanical design of the ORSS module, their expected performance, and initial prototyping results.

Items.Authors: Ellen Schallig, Ian J. Lewis, Alec York, Louis Gabarra, David Terrett, Rui Gao, Gavin Dalton, Diane Chapuis Kerouanton, Thomas Augusteijn, Kacem El Hadi, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Marie Larrieu, Alessandro Meoli, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Myriam Rodrigues, Rubén Sanchez-Janssen, Hermine Schnetler, Jay Stephan, Christian Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC at the ELT: focal plane architecture and initial design
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object fibre spectrograph for ESO’s 39 m Extremely Large Telescope. It covers the visible  (0.39–0.95 µm) and NIR (0.95–1.8 µm) wavelength domains. This paper describes the current architecture of  MOSAIC’s Focal Plane subsystem, a curved support structure that holds about 250 SCARA robots which inject  the telescope light into fixed fibre bundles. We outline the design for each of the main components, including a  carbon-fibre focal plate and an actively cooled focal plane architecture to achieve the required performance. We  also present the control architecture and the software algorithms that perform target allocation and generate  collision-free reconfiguration sequences between observations. Finally, we present some of the prototyping work  done to prepare for assembly and integration.

Items.Authors: Armando Gil de Paz, Ana Pérez Calpena, África Castillo Morales, Marisa García Vargas, Jesús Gallego, Ernesto Sánchez Blanco, Ramón Rodríguez Cardoso, Francisco M. Montenegro-Montes, Mario Chamorro-Cazorla, Rafael González-Fuentetaja
Items.Title: MOSAIC for ELT: CALEMOS: calibration module for the ELT MOS
Items.Abstract: CALEMOS will be the Calibration Module for the MOSAIC instrument, currently under design for the European Large Telescope (ELT). It will provide illumination for the calibration of both its VIS and NIR channels. This MOSAIC sub-system shall incorporate artificial sources for spectral and flat calibration (and should fulfill the ESO-ELT light tightness requirements). Our flat calibrations will require of a continuous, uniform illumination aimed at providing both detector (pixel-to-pixel) and fiber (fiber-to-fiber) flat fielding. The large size of the calibration screen and high incidence angle of the CALEMOS beam are both challenging aspects of its design in terms of both homogeneity and irradiance. In this poster we will also describe the calibration model used to verify those instrument top-level requirements that depend on the performance of both CALEMOS and the MOSAIC calibration and observing strategies.

Items.Authors: Marísa Luisa L. García-Vargas, Ana Pérez-Calpena, Jesús Gallego Maestro, Yevgeniy Ivanisenko, Philippe Laporte, Isabelle Guinouard, Audrey Lanotte, Gerardo Veredas-Luque, Ernesto Sánchez-Blanco Mancera, Manuel Maldonado Medina, María Peñataro-Blanco, Zalpha Challita, Africa Castillo-Morales, José Miguel Ibáñez Mengual, Javier Piqueras López, Armando Gil de Paz, Francois Wildi, Cyril Pannetier, Thomas Augusteijn, Gavin Dalton, Kacem El Hadi, Marie Larrieu, Alessandro Meoli, Roser Pelló, Mathieu Puech, Myriam Rodrigues, Ruben Sanchez-janssen, Hermine Schnetler, Jay Stephan, Christian Surace, Francisco Miguel Montenegro-Montes, Mario Chamorro-Cazorla
Items.Title: MOSAIC for ELT: NIR channel challenges and performance
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object, MOS, spectrograph for the ESO-ELT, designed for a wide range of scientific programs requiring high multiplexing capabilities. MOSAIC enables MOS observations with both low and high spectral resolution (LR and HR), utilizing the ELT’s entire Field of View (FoV, 40 arcmin²). It includes two channels, VIS (0.39 – 0.95 µm) and NIR (0.95 – 1.8 µm), with spectrographs on the Nasmyth platform, all fed by MOS fiber bundles and, in the case of the NIR channel, also by fibers from 8 mIFU sub-apertures. These channels span the full range with a spectral resolution of R ≥ 4,000 in a single exposure and, both also offer an HR mode (R ≥ 18,000). The NIR channel is being designed and developed by universities and research centers from Spain, France and Switzerland. This paper summarizes the challenges, organization and design status of MOSAIC NIR channel in the preliminary design stage.

Items.Authors: A. Perez-Calpena, E. Sanchez-Blanco, M. L. Garcia-Vargas, G. Veredas, M. Maldonado, M. Penataro, J. Gallego, A. Castillo, F. J. Montenegro-Montes, A. Gil de Paz, M. Chamorro-Cazorla, T. Augusteijn, G. Dalton, K. El Hadi, M. Larrieu, A. Meoli, R. Pelló, M. Puech, M. Rodrigues, R. Sanchez-Janssen, H. Schnetler, J. Stephen, C. Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC for ELT: NIR spectrograph system performance
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object and multi-IFU spectrograph for the ESO-ELT in the range 0.39 to 1.8 microns that will provide survey observations. MOSAIC will collect the light from mIFU and MOS subapertures and drive it through the corresponding fiber links to the VIS and NIR spectrographs attached on the Nasmyth platform.   We present the optical and mechanical design and performance of the two NIR identical spectrographs, receiving each half of the fibers from the 180 NIR MOS targets, 630 fibers per spectrograph, and from the 8 mIFU, 672 fibers per spectrograph. Each spectrograph allows simultaneous coverage of J and H bands (0.95 to 1.80 microns) at low resolution (R~4000), and provides high resolution (R~18000) in the H band (1.52 – 1.62 microns). Each spectrograph hosts two cryo-mechanisms: The Entrance Focal Plane, to select between mIFU and MOS slits, an the LR/HR exchanger to select the grating in the H band.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Meoli, Domingo Álvarez Méndez, Elizabeth George, Pablo Alberto Rodriguez, Thomas Augusteijn, Meghna Mohamed, Jay Stephan, Gavin Dalton, Kacem El Hadi, Myriam Rodrigues, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Marie Larrieu, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Christian Surace, Rubén Sánchez Janssen, Hermine Schnetler
Items.Title: MOSAIC on ELT: detector trade-offs for the VIS and NIR channels
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC, the multi-object spectrograph for the ELT, is advancing through its preliminary design phase. Its distributed architecture, with over twenty-five interconnected subsystems, places stringent demands on the detector systems, which strongly influence optical throughput, focal-plane geometry, and thermal/electronic performance. We present a coordinated assessment of the visible (VIS) and near-infrared (NIR) detector options. For VIS, we examine large-format CCD technologies and the trade-off between quantum efficiency and focal-plane tiling constraints. For NIR, we compare H4RG configurations and their behaviour at 40 K and 80 K. The study outlines how each option shapes performance, risk, and integration complexity for the next MOSAIC design phases.

Items.Authors: Gavin B. Dalton, Myriam Rodrigues, Roser Pello, Kacem El Hadi, Mathieu Puech, Jurgen Schmoll, Jeff Lynn, Thomas Augusteijn, Meghna Mohamed, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Ana Pérez Calpena, Walter Seifert, Wenli Xu, Ruben Sanchez-Janssen, Jay Stephan, Ian Lewis, Alondra Sola-Molina, Alessandro Meoli, Markus Thurneysen
Items.Title: MOSAIC, the ELT multiobject spectrograph: development and evolution of the instrument architecture and capabilities
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object spectrograph (MOS) for the 39-meter Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) of the European Southern Observatory (ESO). We present the evolution of the instrument concept from its initial conception through to the final design concept that will be presented at PDR. The evolution of the design by incorporation of per-target compensation for atmospheric dispersion has provided a route to conformance with tight restrictions on mass and volume, whilst at the same time expanding the overall efficiency of the instrument in terms of functionality and information gathering power.

Items.Authors: Jürgen Schmoll, Diane Chapuis-Kerouanton, Gavin Dalton, Louis Gabarra, Malak Galal, Ian Lewis, Myriam Rodrigues, Maxime Rombach, Daniel P. Sablowski, Ellen Schallig, Markus Thurneysen, Alec York
Items.Title: MOSAIC, the ELT multiobject spectrograph: positioners with integrated atmospheric dispersion correction
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the multi-object fibre spectrograph for ESO's 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). It offers unique capabilities for a gigantic telescope in terms of multiplexing, wavelength coverage and spectral resolution. MOSAIC covers the visible (0.39-0.95 microns) and NIR (0.95-1.8 microns) wavelength domains. It has been designed to cover the largest possible area (~40 arcmin²) on the ELT focal plane.  This paper focuses on the optical realisation of the robotic arms designed to pick the light from the curved, non-telecentric focal surface while providing individual atmospheric dispersion correction for each of the 261 probes. Further challenges of the design are the large wavelength range and the tight tolerances necessary for an efficient optical fibre injection. An optical setup to test prototypes and to characterize the batch produced positioners will be introduced, allowing each individual pickoff arm to reach the tight tolerances for pointing accuracy and pupil stability.

Items.Authors: Lulu Qian, Min Huang, Guangming Wang, Yixin Zhao, Zhanchao Wang
Items.Title: Near Space Balloon-based Corona Observation Payload Design and Analysis
Items.Abstract: This paper introduces the design and analysis of the coronal observation payload cabin. To ensure the safe recovery of the observation payload when the payload module lands after the experiment, a finite element-based impact mechanics analysis was carried out. The simulation results show that the design of the payload module can effectively mitigate the landing impact and provide reliable protection for the payload. On this basis, we conducted a flight experiment, achieving a flight altitude of 30 km and a flight duration of approximately 3 hours. The experiment results indicate that the payload module functioned properly, effectively guaranteeing the data acquisition of the coronal observation payload. After the experiment, the coronagraph landed in good condition with normal functionality..

Items.Authors: Karen Tateoka, Hayato Takakura, Yutaro Sekimoto, Junji Inatani, Rion Takahashi, Frederick Matsuda, Shugo Oguri
Items.Title: Near-field polarisation angle measurement for wide field-of-view millimeter-wave telescopes
Items.Abstract: Accurate calibration of a telescope's polarisation angle is crucial for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) B-mode observations to mitigate the leakage from E-mode.    In this work, we investigate a polarisation angle calibration method based on a near-field measurement.  The amplitude and phase distributions scanned on a plane near the aperture were Fourier-transformed to obtain the antenna patterns, including the far sidelobes.  We present the polarisation angles of a crossed-Dragone telescope, determined from the measured co- and cross-polarisation patterns.    By employing holographic phase-retrieval techniques (R. Takahashi et al., 2024, Proc. SPIE, 13102), near-field measurements can be performed on a telescope with bolometric detectors such as LiteBIRD.  It offers the prospect of reconstructing the antenna patterns of thousands of detectors within a single scan.

Items.Authors: R. Pellegrini, P. Gregori, F. Cerutti, F. Diprima, J. Mura, E. Dölling, E. Cordelli, L. Conversi, D. Föhring
Items.Title: NEO Flyeye network: from the commissioning of the OHB-I Flyeye-1 to the future Flyeye-2 deployment
Items.Abstract: The Flyeye telescope, developed by OHB Italia for ESA’s Space Safety Programme, achieved first light in May 2025, becoming the first operational compound-eye survey telescope for planetary defence. Its 1m mirror feeds 16 independent channels, achieving 1.5arcsec/px resolution and a 45deg² FoV, enabling high-cadence, wide-area coverage that traditional narrow-field telescopes cannot provide.   Commissioning activities at ASI Matera site validated system integration, detectors synchronization and data-flow, with successful detections of known NEO, even if not yet operating at nominal alignment. After acceptance, Flyeye will be installed on Mt. Mufara by late 2026 as key element of ESA’s NEO survey. The NEO survey strategy foresees to image each field four times per night with ~20-minute revisits, covering the visible sky to V≈21.5 every 2–3 nights and significantly improving warning times for 10-40m size impactors.  A second-generation Flyeye is planned for Chile to enhance global coverage

Items.Authors: Camilo Weinberger, Elena Masciadri, Marlène de Sepibus, Angel Otarola, Steffen Mieske, Christian Veillet, Sam Ragland
Items.Title: Neural networks applied to forecasting the astroclimatic parameters in an operational context
Items.Abstract: The forecasting of optical turbulence is a crucial goal for astronomical ground-based observations for science operational optimization. Current research in this area identified autoregressive (AR) models as the best performers so far, achieving an RMSE of about 0.1″ for seeing forecasts on a time scale of 1h however neural networks (NN) remain extremely appealing as they are very flexible and they can be applied in contexts where the AR can not be used. It is therefore interesting to investigate characteristics of such an approach particularly in a forecasting operational context. We extend here our analysis to current NN algorithms beyond RF specifically developed for time series therefore for the forecast context. Our goals are to identify the best performances achievable with neural networks and the best operational configuration. This study is carried out within the framework of the FATE and ALTA projects, applied respectively to the VLT and LBT.

Items.Authors: Matthias Seidel, Alexander Rüde, Mathias Richerzhagen
Items.Title: NGCII detector controller synchronization using the White Rabbit protocol
Items.Abstract: Accurate synchronization between detector controllers is relevant for low-noise readout in focal-plane arrays. ESO’s new detector controller NGCII uses White Rabbit to enable sub-nanosecond timing accuracy and timestamp distribution in a PTP environment. In this presentation, we describe the method used to integrate White Rabbit into the NGCII architecture and show first lab results.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Umbriaco, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Maria Bergomi, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Thomas M. Herbst, Remon van Gaalen, Roberto Ragazzoni, Valentina Viotto, Luca Cortese, Jacopo Farinato, Luca Marafatto, Silvio Di Rosa, Marco Dima, Davide Greggio, Florian Briegel, Lars Mohr, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Simone Antoniucci, Al Conrad, Alessio Caratti O. Garatti, Gianluca Li Causi, Fabrizio Massi, Fernando Pedichini, Roberto Piazzesi, Sam Ragland
Items.Title: NirvanaVIS at LBT: AO-assisted speckle holography for wide-field visible imaging
Items.Abstract: High-angular-resolution imaging from ground-based telescopes is limited by atmospheric turbulence and speckle decorrelation. Speckle holography and bispectrum phase retrieval complement adaptive optics (AO), extending diffraction-limited imaging toward wider fields and fainter targets.  NirvanaVIS is a visible-band imaging camera planned for LBT, operating with the ground-layer correction from LINC-NIRVANA. It will provide a stable, uniform PSF across a 52'' x 52'' field, 600-1000 nm.  We review the main Fourier-based speckle reconstruction techniques for AO-assisted visible imaging and present simulations of the GLAO-corrected PSF for NirvanaVIS on the GJ 15 b and NGC 7914 fields. Simulations show that GLAO-assisted speckle holography can recover diffraction-limited imaging at 20-40 mas, sensitive to companions fainter than the reference sources.  A Python pipeline is under development, validated on Copernico 1.82 m data and the Ekarus AO bench, ahead of NirvanaVIS deployment at LBT.

Items.Authors: Jonathan Dray, Kyliann Robert, Cyril Petit, Morgan Gray, Jalo Nousiainen, Romain Fetick, Baptiste Sinquin, Hisham Forrière, Armin Schimpf, Julien Charton, Thierry Fusco, Benoit Neichel
Items.Title: Numerical comparisons of VAR LQG-based predictive AO control and reinforcement-learning–based control methods for LEO-to-ground telecommunication links
Items.Abstract: In the field of adaptive optics for telecommunications with LEO satellites, new control methods emerge to counteract the specific turbulence effects encountered for these types of optical links. Here, we propose to compare numerically, with  end-to-end simulations, VAR LQG control and reinforcement-learning-based control in a variety of turbulence conditions.

Items.Authors: Romain J. L. Fétick, Arnaud Striffling, Matteo Pasinetti, Vincent Chambouleyron, Taissir Héritier
Items.Title: Observation of extended objects with a pyramid wavefront sensor: on-sky validation with the PAPYRUS AO system
Items.Abstract: The pyramid wavefront sensor (WFS) high sensitivity makes it the perfect candidate for future instruments such as the European ELT/HARMONI, or the French OHP/PROVIDENCE with satellite tracking ability. However, the object spatial extension dramatically reduces the pyramid sensitivity, even questioning its usage on extended objects.    We present here the loss of sensitivity due to object extension and show the possibility to compensate for the optical gains and retrieve the aberrant turbulence phase with fidelity for improved AO performances. We show the possibility to use the pyramid WFS on extended object through simulations, but also thanks to on-sky experiments with the PAPYRUS adaptive optics bench installed at Observatoire de Haute Provence.    The first results validate the use of a GSC for future instruments such as PCS to be installed at ELT. It also provides a baseline for operations of the pyramid WFS on extended objects with applications for HARMONI or PROVIDENCE.

Items.Authors: Luis Caniguante, Jorge Ramírez
Items.Title: Obsolescence-driven upgrade of the VLT M1 cell earthquake detector using a COTS and functional safety strategy
Items.Abstract: The Earthquake Detector (EQD) protects the VLT’s primary mirror (M1) during strong seismic events or abnormal mechanical motion. The M1 mirrors are unique optical components produced specifically for the VLT, making reliable protection essential. After more than twenty years of service, the original EQD became highly obsolete due to aging custom electronics and unavailable spare parts. This work presents a complete upgrade of the EQD using modern Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) technologies and a fail-safe PLC platform. The new design improves reliability, simplifies maintenance, and ensures long-term operability. By maintaining the protection of a key optical component, the upgraded EQD contributes to the sustained performance and operational continuity of the VLT.

Items.Authors: Aditi Gangadharan, Drew M. Miles, James H. Tutt, Jake A. McCoy, Ross C. McCurdy, Alexandra N. Higley, Randall L. McEntaffer
Items.Title: OGREs can see: synchrotron-based diffraction efficiency testing of OGRE diffraction gratings
Items.Abstract: The Off-plane Grating Rocket Experiment (OGRE) is a sounding rocket mission designed to obtain high-resolution soft X-ray spectra of Capella in the 0.2-2.0 keV band while demonstrating next-generation technologies for soft X-ray spectroscopy. A central enabling technology for the payload is modules of radially profiled, blazed off-plane reflection gratings. Achieving high diffraction efficiency, specifically a minimum design target of ~40% near 825 eV, is essential for meeting OGRE’s spectral throughput requirements. We present the methodology and results of absolute diffraction-efficiency measurements for multiple prototype variants of the OGRE master grating, performed at the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. These prototypes sample variations in grating geometry and blaze configuration as part of an iterative optimization process toward the mission’s efficiency goals. The measurements reported here provide key performance metrics that guide the ongoing

Items.Authors: Claudio Arena, Giuseppe Leto, Alessio Trois, Julien Cailleaux, Vito Conforti, Gianluca Giavitto, Luigi Lessio, Giovanni Lombardo, Cesare Molfese, Nicola La Palombara, Salvatore Scuderi, Gino Tosti
Items.Title: On-factory testing of the SST Telescopes for CTAO
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will be composed of two arrays of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, with three different types of telescopes. The small-sized telescopes (SSTs, 37 units) are developed by an international consortium of institutes that will provide them as an in-kind contribution to CTAO. SSTs will be installed in Paranal (Chile) as part of the South site.    In this contribution we present the initial AIT/V activities carried out on the first SST units, with a focus on the on-factory test campaign. The activities span from safety aspects of the SSTs, testing of the various interfaces, functional and performance validation, and the evaluation of maintenance procedures foreseen during CTAO operations.  The AIT/V workflow is framed within the heritage of the ASTRI program, with a focus on how on-factory activities simplify and de-risk the subsequent on-site testing, verification and commissioning phases.

Items.Authors: Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Jared Males, Parker Johnson, Laird Close, Olivier Guyon, Joseph Long, Jay Kueny, Joshua Liberman, Miles Lucas, Eden McEwen, Tiffany Nguyen, Adam Taras, Kyle Van Gorkom, Maggie Kautz, Katie Twitchell, Lauren Schatz
Items.Title: On-sky demonstration of self-learning predictive control with MagAO-X
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of exoplanets is very tricky and requires extremely well corrected wavefronts. Especially low-order order modes are detrimental to the performance of coronagraphs at their inner-working angle. However, that is precisely where conventional AO systems have the highest residuals that are caused by servo-lag errors. This servo-lag error can be reduced with predictive control where the control anticipates the future state of the atmospheric disturbance. We use a self-learning model predictive controller based on the concepts from sub-space predictive control (SPC). We present a novel implementation of the SPC by using an online QR-decomposition based recursive least squares approach. This approach has now been used for self-learning control of vibrations on the MagAO-X instrument. We see on average an Strehl increase of 15 percent and a decrease of the jitter from 3 mas to 0.9 mas. I will discuss how we have implemented the controller and its on-sky perfomance.

Items.Authors: Francesco Di Mille, Marcelo Mora, Guillermo Blanc, David Osip, Povilas Palunas
Items.Title: Operational status and instrument suite development at the Magellan Telescopes
Items.Abstract: The Magellan telescopes at Las Campanas Observatory continue to evolve as the Carnegie Institution for Science partnership with Harvard/Smithsonian CfA, the University of Arizona, MIT, and the University of Michigan passes twenty years of operations. We present an updated view of the instrumentation suite and science operations at the 6.5-m Baade and Clay telescopes. Baade now hosts five permanently mounted, always-available instruments. At Clay, the second Nasmyth port is being converted from a fixed to a flexible interface to support longer, more continuous instrument availability. Over the past two years, three IFU instruments have been integrated, significantly expanding spatially resolved spectroscopy. We summarize recent performance trends, reliability considerations, and operational lessons from this configuration, and outline ongoing modernization efforts to meet the evolving needs of the Magellan user community.

Items.Authors: Anthony J. Shipp, Abigail Heins, Ethan Pascuales, Joshua A. Franklin, Keller Powell, Julian Pallini, Maria A. Chytka, Cailin Bain, Carter Stevens, Samuel G. Arnold, Gang Wang
Items.Title: Optical characterization and field testing of InfraTracker: next generation near infrared and visible light star tracker for suborbital sounding rocket flight
Items.Abstract: InfraTracker delivers a low-cost, first of its kind visible and infrared light star tracker assembly that increases performance while lowering resource usage for the cutting edge of defense and space research. The mission is focused on designing a compact, low-cost, and reusable star tracker using visible to near infrared light, from primarily COTS components. InfraTracker will utilize a Terrier-Improved Malemute sounding rocket out of NASA Wallops Flight Facility (WFF) as part of the RockSat program, allowing for observations to be made above most of Earth’s atmosphere allowing for flight qualification in space.

Items.Authors: Megan M. Dubay, Thomas Procter, William Marshall, Hank Corbett, Nicholas M. Law, Jonah L. Aponte, Alex Bucheli, Jonathan Carney, Thomas Cowart, James Dockery, Katie M. Fasbender, Shannon Fitton, Collin H. Grimes, Amy S. Ishiguro, Lawrence Machia, Michael Ronco, Donovan G. Schlekat, Alan Vasquez Soto, Glenn Walters
Items.Title: Optical performance verification for the Argus Array
Items.Abstract: The Argus Array is an all-sky survey instrument with the effective area of an 8m telescope. It will image 8,000sq-degrees of sky as often as once a second. Detailed optical simulations show that the 1200-telescope array will reach at least magnitude g=20.0 in a single 60s exposure with 1.0” pixel scale. Prior to beginning full production, we performed several tests of the optical and imaging components as verification of the predicted performance for the integrated system, effects on performance for varying atmospheric conditions, and as a validation of the design. Testing of the prototype units of the f/2.8 28cm OTAs and custom 100-megapixel IMX461 cameras occurred at McDonald Observatory and at Argus facilities. Here we discuss the equipment, testing procedures, analysis methods, and findings.

Items.Authors: Grace Piroscia, Connor Langford, Peter Tuthill, Christopher Betters, Frans Snik, Louis Desdoigts, Benjamin Pope, David Doelman
Items.Title: Optical testbed and performance evaluation of large liquid-crystal diffractive optics
Items.Abstract: The TOLIMAN space telescope mission targets revolutionary performance in precision astrometric monitoring of binary stars to detect orbiting companions at micro-arcsecond levels of precision. A key enabling technology is a 125mm diameter patterned diffractive transmission plate with precisely aligned liquid crystal (LC) axes. Assembly of the flight-ready LC TOLIMAN poses immediate challenges to maintain optical transmitted wavefront quality. Along with this, LC polarisation degradation due to temperature and UV exposure is not well understood in an Earth orbit context. Using an optical testbed at the University of Sydney, this paper presents methodologies and outcomes in the pathway to furnish a flight-qualified LC diffractive pupil.

Items.Authors: Alireza Vafa, Alireza Basohbat Novinzadeh, Mahshid Shiri
Items.Title: Optical/IR interferometry in space: evolution of concepts and missions
Items.Abstract: This paper reviews the evolution of space interferometry in optical and infrared domains from its theoretical foundations to contemporary mission concepts. Early developments, including Bracewell’s nulling interferometer and Labeyrie’s hypertelescope, established the principles of high contrast exoplanet detection and ultra high resolution imaging. We examine major mission concepts such as Darwin, TPF, SIM, Stellar Imager, ST3/StarLight, SPIRIT, and SPECS, highlighting their scientific objectives, architectures, and implementation challenges. We also review technological advances achieved during the 2010s, including precision formation flying, metrology, nulling interferometry, and ground based testbeds. Finally, we discuss recent initiatives such as LIFE and emerging architectures based on lunar and CubeSat platforms. The field has evolved from visionary concepts toward a technology driven roadmap for future space interferometers.

Items.Authors: Ludwig von Dossow, Emilio Barrios, Héctor Alarcón, Patricio Álvarez, Eduardo Chaparro, Emiliano Galuppo, Christian García, Daniela Soto
Items.Title: Optimizing the Control Room environment: A review of teamwork and implementation stages at the ALMA Observatory
Items.Abstract: The construction and commissioning of observatory control rooms involve critical design stages. The ALMA Observatory has undertaken this process twice: for its remote control room in Santiago and, recently, for a new Operations Support Facility (OSF) room housing the ATAC correlator.    Beyond technical specifications, post-commissioning improvements focused on human factors were achieved through essential teamwork. The Array Operations Group consolidated feedback from diverse users, including Engineering and Outreach departments, to optimize the workspace. This paper reviews the resulting operational enhancements and demonstrates how this collaborative approach created a superior operating environment, providing valuable considerations for other scientific facilities.

Items.Authors: Yue Yu, Jooyun Woo, Ipek Altunyurt, Stefano Basso, Vadim Burwitz, Francisco R. Candón, Juan F. Castel Pablo, Marta M. Civitani, Todd Decker, Klaus Desch, Desiree D. M. Ferreira, Javier Galan, Maurizio Giannotti, Louis Helary, Peter L. Henriksen, Igor G. Irastorza, Eftychia Kotsiou, Axel Lindner, Frank Marutzky, Sonny Massahi, Sam Moseley, Takashi Okajima, Johanna von Oy, Diego Paredes-Sanz, Giancarlo Parodi, Marcela Stern, Kerstin Perez, Michael J. Pivovaroff, David Reuther, Jaime Ruz Armendariz, Anacorina Romero, Vyshnavi Sabbi, Tobias Schiffer, Uwe Schneekloth, Julia K. Vogel, Daniele Spiga
Items.Title: Overview and design optimization of a custom hybrid X-ray telescope for the International Axion Observatory (IAXO)
Items.Abstract: Axions and axion-like particles (ALPs) are among the most compelling candidates for dark matter. The International Axion Observatory (IAXO) is a next-generation axion helioscope designed to search for axions and ALPs from the Sun that are reconverted into X-ray photons via strong magnetic fields, while BabyIAXO, a preliminary pathfinder experiment, will validate all key technologies at scale. Among the technologies, the focusing X-ray telescopes are essential to both take advantage of dramatically increased magnetic field volumes and to improve the signal-to-noise ratio at the detector. We present the design optimization, performance evaluation, and fabrication error budget of a cost-effective, scalable hybrid optic for BabyIAXO. Compared to CAST, this optic increases the effective area by 2–3 orders of magnitude across a wider energy range, and achieves a PSF angular HPD of ~46'' for an infinite point source and a focal spot HPD of ~120'' for an extended source.

Items.Authors: Florian Kerber, Rául Cordero, Omar Cuevas, Susana Deustua, Patricio Galeas, Markus Gaug, Rory Gillespie, Miska Le Louarn, Julio C. Marin, Ricardo C. Munoz, Angel Otarola, Anna Francesca Pala, Jérôme Paufique, Joseph P. Rice, Roberto Rondanelli, Alain Smette, Roberta Zanin
Items.Title: PARABOLAS: profiling of the atmosphere by remote sensing and radiosonde balloon launches above our astronomical observatory sites
Items.Abstract: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) is teaming up with international partners to conduct a measurement campaign with the main objective of characterizing a significant volume of atmosphere above the Paranal (VLT), Armazones (ELT) and the future Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) South sites covering a horizontal distance of about 25 km between the observatory sites and an altitude of at least 15 km to address both its spatial and temporal variations using an array of in-situ and remote sensing instrumentation. The campaign’s results will be key for the science operations of ESO’s fully adaptive Extremely Large Telescope, and highly relevant for the NIST Stars project on Paranal, and for the CTAO which uses the atmosphere as its detection medium for gamma rays. The campaign is currently scheduled for 2026/27. We’ll report on the current status of planning and the next steps towards the actual implementation.

Items.Authors: Ioannis Argyriou, Roy van Boekel, Alistair C. H. Glasse, Eckhart Spalding, Danny Gasman, Daniel Dicken, Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Oliver Czoske, Gilles Otten, Hugo Buddelmeijer, Janus D. Brink, Wolfgang Brandner, Jennifer L. Karr, Benjamin Eisele, Kieran Leschinski, Wim De Meester, Kwinten Missiaen, Bernhard R. Brandl
Items.Title: Paving the road to the top: Preparations for the ELT-METIS system performance test campaign
Items.Abstract: The Mid-Infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) - first light instrument for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) - is in the process of assembly and integration in Leiden, The Netherlands. Following integration and alignment, the METIS (high-contrast) imaging and spectroscopic mode performance will be tested using the Warm Calibration Unit and Telescope Simulator. The vast number of METIS instrument configurations makes testing the performance of all the modes a unique challenge. Thankfully the instrument simulator ScopeSim allows to produce radiometrically-representative METIS detector images of the calibration sources for each mode. These data are used to develop the analysis tools, define test sequences, and determine initial exposure parameters. In this work we present the logical flow of the performance tests that will be carried out in Leiden as well as simulated data and performance analysis tools that will create the foundation for the activities in Europe and in Chile.

Items.Authors: Thomas Lechner, Todd Veach, Cynthia Froning, Adam Thornton, Andrew Peterson, Trent Peterson, Dana Koeppe
Items.Title: Performance and NIR detector characterization of SCORPIO for the Gemini South Observatory
Items.Abstract: SCORPIO is a multi-channel optical-infrared instrument for the Gemini South 8-meter telescope, providing spectroscopy (0.385-2.35 µm) and imaging (0.400-2.35 µm) across eight synchronized focal plane arrays. The system uses four Teledyne H2RG HgCdTe detectors and four Teledyne e2v CCDs, read out via archon and SIDECAR/MACIE electronics. A custom synchronization backplane distributes a master clock and triggers to all detectors, enabling 10 ms timing precision and 50 ms temporal resolution for rapid transient science. We present ongoing detector performance characterization, including H2RG response, readout stability, and cross-channel synchronization, as SCORPIO progresses towards integration and deployment at Gemini South.

Items.Authors: Viktoria Kutnohorsky, Robert J. Harris, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Laird M. Close, Jared R. Males, Aurelien Benoit, David MacLachlan, Robert R. Thomson, Tim Birks, Chiara D'Amato, Sajjad Mahdizadeh, Andrea Bianco, Giorgio Pariani, Joss Guy, Olivier Guyon
Items.Title: Performance estimates and target selection for the MCIFU, the multicore integrated field unit
Items.Abstract: The Multi-Core Integrated Field Unit (MCIFU) is a demonstrator for the ELT’s Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS) and will achieve first light in 2026 on MagAO-X at the Magellan Clay telescope. To evaluate its performance, we developed a quantitative model incorporating atmospheric transmission, telescope and instrument throughput, and detector characteristics such as quantum efficiency, dark current, and readout noise. Based on this model, an exposure time calculator (ETC) was constructed to predict the signal-to-noise ratio under varying stellar magnitudes, integration times, and observing conditions. The ETC includes three source-spectrum options: continuum, blackbody, and reference spectra. It produces detailed SNR budgets across the Y, J, and H bands to identify observable targets. First-light photometric measurements in 2026 will aide to validate the model and help define the operational parameter space for future PCS observations on the ELT.

Items.Authors: Paul Hickson, Kuntal Misra, Jean Surdej, Bhavya Ailawadhi, Monalisa Dubey, Naveen Dukiya, Priyanshi Kumari, Gokul Singh Mehra, Vibhore Negi, Anna Pospieszalska-Surdej, Kumar Pranshu, Sarvesh Kumar Yadav
Items.Title: Performance of the International Liquid Mirror Telescope
Items.Abstract: The International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) is a 4-meter zenith-pointing astronomical survey telescope. Located at Devasthal Peak in the Indian Himalayas, the project is a collaboration between institutions in Belgium, India and Canada. Its primary scientific program is the detection and study of transient and variable sources. A unique feature of the ILMT is its primary mirror which employs liquid mercury as the reflecting surface. Equipped with a 4096 x 4096 pixel CCD camera, the telescope records images of a 22.4 arcmin wide strip of sky passing overhead, revisiting every object in the strip each night for several months. The ILMT began operation in 2022, and has now obtained over 1900 hours of imaging data. We provide an overview of the project and discuss the performance of the telescope, including image quality, limiting magnitudes, observing statistics, data products and the transient detection success rate.

Items.Authors: Romain Laugier, Lucas Labadie, Denis Defrère, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Guillermo Martin
Items.Title: Phase-sensing with the modified Mach-Zehnder nuller
Items.Abstract: Integrated-optics tricouplers are one of the rare nulling beam-combiners that can provide phase sensing in operation, but they lack a bulk optics equivalent.  With this work, we demonstrate how this sensing ability arises in the beam combination, and how it fundamentally comes at the cost of off-axis light. We then propose a novel alteration to the modified Mach-Zehnder topology (Serabyn 2001) of balanced beamsplitter to bring sensing capabilities by recycling light already shed by the combiner to balance intensity at no additional throughput cost. This new option offers a pivotal new architecture options for fine piston control accuracy and null maintenance with reduced overheads.

Items.Authors: Hirofumi Okita, Naoyuki Tamura, Takashi Hattori, Yuhei Takagi, Yusei Koyama, Masayuki Kuzuhara, Hatsune Uekiyo
Items.Title: PI-type instrumentation at the Subaru Telescope
Items.Abstract: We explain the PI-type Instrumentation program at the Subaru Telescope. The Subaru Telescope has a framework for PI-type instruments, which are developed, assembled, integrated, tested, and operated using external funding and human resources to achieve specific science goals or demonstrate novel technology, and which complement with facility instruments that are developed, maintained, and operated by resources of the Subaru Telescope. In this paper, we briefly explain outline and uniqueness of the PI-type instrumentation program at the Subaru Telescope, as well as the brief summary of the approval process of the PI-type instruments and current problems. We will also summarize the results of the productivity study and user opinions survey discussed at the PI-type instrument workshop held in October 2025.

Items.Authors: Jaya Chand
Items.Title: Polaris and Zenith non-tracking Differential Image Motion Monitors for robust atmospheric turbulence monitoring
Items.Abstract: Traditional DIMM seeing monitors depend on bright stars and accurate tracking mounts, increasing system cost, complexity, and maintenance.To address this, we present two wide-field, static, untracked DIMMs: the Polaris DIMM and the Zenith DIMM.These instruments aim to provide reliable Fried parameter measurements with minimal infrastructure and autonomous operation.The Polaris DIMM continuously observes Polaris without tracking but cannot operate in equatorial regions or the southern hemisphere.To achieve global applicability, the Zenith DIMM uses an even larger field of view with fixed pointing to function at any latitude.Both prototypes were installed on the ING DIMM tower at ORM, La Palma, where they showed good agreement with the ING robotic DIMM (R2D2).Using scintillation index and covariance, we also estimate a simple three-layer turbulence profile, from which the isoplanatic angle, and with wind information, the coherence time and photometric scintillation noise, can be derived.

Items.Authors: Federico Astori
Items.Title: POLOCALC and HoverCal drone system: attitude reconstruction software
Items.Abstract: Precise calibration of the absolute polarization angle is critical for detecting primordial B-mode signals in the cosmic microwave background. The POLOCALC and HoverCal projects operate drone-borne polarized microwave emitters (90–280 GHz) to provide a stable far-field reference for telescopes. The key innovation is the use of photogrammetry, tightly integrated with onboard sensors, to determine the drone’s attitude with extreme precision, directly linking the orientation of the emitted polarization signal to fixed ground references. Leveraging this technique, the system aims to achieve absolute polarization angle calibration with an accuracy of σΨ ~ 0.01°, sufficient for searching primordial B-modes at the level σ_r ~ 10⁻³. Photogrammetry is central to determining the polarization plane’s orientation in celestial coordinates, employing a sophisticated color-filtering algorithm and a Bayesian framework to retrieve the drone’s attitude within these stringent accuracy requirements.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Cotroneo, Giovanni Pareschi, Stefano Basso, Marta M. Civitani, Thorsten Dohring, Eugenio Gibertini, Giorgia Sironi, Daniele Spiga
Items.Title: Polydopamine overcoatings for soft X-ray reflectivity enhancements: recent progress and performance assessment
Items.Abstract: We present recent advances in dopamine-based overcoatings to enhance the soft X-ray performance of grazing-incidence telescope mirrors. Thin polydopamine (PDA) films, deposited by dip-coating from aqueous solution, provide a carbon-rich, low-density layer on conventional high-Z coatings (e.g. Au, Ir, Ir/Cr), offering an attractive, lower-cost alternative to sputtered carbon or other carbon-based films (e.g. SiC, B₄C). We report an expanded set of laboratory and synchrotron reflectivity measurements, together with process optimization (thickness control, uniformity, reproducibility), tests on relevant mirror geometries, and an assessment of surface roughness and small-angle scattering. Ongoing environmental and adhesion studies, combined with updated optical modelling, support the potential application of these coatings in future cost-constrained spaceborne X-ray telescopes requiring large effective area in the soft band.

Items.Authors: Michael Mann, Thorsten Döhring, Alessandro Priebsch, Udo Sauer, Alexander Stock, Georgios Fotis
Items.Title: Power quality diagnostics at astronomical observatories
Items.Abstract: Astronomical observatories supplied by long radial grids are highly susceptible to power quality disturbances. Conventional monitoring based on 10‑minute RMS aggregation systematically suppresses fast transient and subtransient phenomena, although these directly affect electromagnetic compatibility and measurement stability.  This work introduces a diagnostic methodology using transient recorders for synchronized, microsecond‑resolution measurements of voltage and current across phase, neutral, and protective earth conductors. The approach combines time‑domain analysis with frequency‑dependent impedance characterization.  Experimental results show that fast events with significant amplitudes occur and are governed by grid impedance, while remaining invisible in standardized PQ metrics. The methodology provides a physically interpretable extension of conventional power quality assessment for weak and inverter‑dominated systems.
